analysis:
Examined the Flint request-control plumbing in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine+Translation.swift (head 23-93, 172-208) and the patch to MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift.

Changes:
- ChatTemplateControls gains `rawFlintControls`, copied in `withPromptDate` and settable via `withRawFlintControls`. The existing `rawMiMoControls`/`rawGLM5Controls` copying is unchanged. Synthesized Equatable now also covers the Flint evidence.
- `translate` gains `engineStopStrings` (default true), so default behavior is unchanged for existing callers. The scheduler passes `modelType != "flint"`, so `stop` is withheld from the engine for Flint and enforced by a `FlintAnswerStopFilter` applied to raw text before the router and tool parsing. The filter is also flushed at stream end.
- `FlintRequestPolicy.validate` already runs in `prepareCompletion` (line 449 of base, unchanged). The read-only resident model-type lookup at line 327 now also triggers on invalid Flint controls. This lookup does not load or provision models, and it preserves the existing cold-model and cancellation handling.
- New `withholdReasoning` and `usageSignal.recordWithheldReasoning` run before later frames, so billing and usage still see the withheld tokens. `FlintResponseFormatOutput.validate(finishReason:)` fails the stream and fires `releaseBox` on invalid or truncated output. The matched-stop path sets stopReason to "stop".

No concrete regression was found against the cited threats (T-008, T-010, T-041). The sealed-body overlay for seed/logit_bias stays authoritative. No plaintext-on-encryption-failure path and no cache-scope change is introduced in the visible diff. Release-box handling on the new error paths looks consistent.

Unverified contracts (not findings):
- The `FlintRequestPolicy`, `FlintAnswerStopConstraint`, `FlintAnswerStopFilter` and `FlintResponseFormatOutput` implementations were not supplied.
- The code that builds `tokenConstraint` was not supplied. Line 901 of head makes `answerStopFilter` depend on `tokenConstraint` being a `FlintAnswerStopConstraint`, while engine stops are dropped on `modelType == "flint"`. If a flint-typed model ever lacks that constraint, `stop` would be silently ignored. This affects correctness and possibly generation length and resource use, not confidentiality. The "exact Flint" gating needs confirmation.
- Where `rawFlintControls` is populated (the ProviderLoop sealed-body decode) was not supplied.
- The max-length and buffering bounds of the stop holdback were not visible.
